pages.text: Every block a printer places is paid for in $(l)Filament Units (FU)$(). To make FU, feed raw materials into a $(item)Filament Winder$() to wind them onto a $(item)Filament Spool$(), then Shift+Right Click the spool onto a printer's $(l)side$().$(br2)A material's FU value is derived from its crafting / smelting recipe graph, so the economy stays self-consistent.
A Tier 1 spool holds $(l)500 FU$(). Higher tiers hold far more (see FU Economy).

pages.title: Exact-Tier Winding
pages.text: The winder is strict: a material only winds into a spool of its $(l)exact tier$(). Netherite (Tier 5) needs a Tier 5 spool; cobblestone (Tier 1) needs a Tier 1 spool.$(br2)This is deliberate — it stops cheap, mass-farmed blocks from ever filling a high-tier spool and undercutting the economy.

pages.title: Spending FU
pages.text: At print time the rule relaxes one way: a spool can pay any cost $(l)at or below$() its own tier, never above. High-tier FU covers low-tier blocks (down-converted at the configured ratio); low-tier FU contributes $(l)nothing$() toward higher-tier blocks.$(br2)So a stack of Tier 5 spools can print a whole stone house, but a Tier 1 spool can never print netherite.
